added_claim_errors: Fraud/proxy-exam penalty given as '1000–2000 元' (第三十一条): the article says fraud is 1000元以下 and impersonation 2000元以下, so the range is wrong (I opened the gov.cn text of the 办法).

Time table is internally inconsistent: components of 30 + 10–20 + 5–15 min sum to 45–65 min per round, but the table says '约50–70分钟'. Stated '理论下限5小时' even though 3 h study + 6×10 min exam is 4 h. The 5–15 min overhead per round is invented.
'每天 2–3 次，2–3 天减满 6 分': no official source for several applications per day or for the 2–3 day pace (the key warns about timing claims). Unverifiable.
Specific UI wording ('在线申请', 首页驾驶证卡片上的'可减分', '去学习', '去考试', '网办进度') is stated as fact for all provinces. Unverifiable; only '更多→学习教育业务→学法减分' and 网上学习 are backed by the Beijing page I opened.
Face recognition 'usually gives 2 chances, two failures void the attempt': the Beijing page confirms random capture but not the 2-chance rule. Unverifiable.
Shenzhen and Qingdao police links cited for the exclusion list and the on-site/public-benefit rules were not opened; the content matches the 办法 text, which I did check.
Exam 'total 20 minutes' and 'three wrong/unanswered = automatic fail' are not on the Beijing page I opened (the 18/20 pass mark is in the key). A makes the same claims; unverifiable.
Step 1 '打开12123→首页→驾驶证，确认累积记分和清分日期' and '系统提交申请时会校验' are UI/behaviour details I could not verify.
Step list has no review/approval step after applying and no face recognition at the application step (the key lists both). This is an omission, not a false statement.
Exam time 'at most 5 hours' treats 20 min as the cap per exam; plausible given the stated limit, but the 20-minute limit itself is unverified.

reasons: Both answers open by saying the cap is 6 points and not 10. Both explain the 4-point leftover, the 8-point risk of reaching 12, and the rule that points clear at the cycle end if under 12 and fines are paid. Both also give the 30-minute, 20-question, 18-to-pass, 2-retake details, and a correct list of ineligibility conditions. I checked the 办法 text on gov.cn (Articles 15, 17, 18, 25, 26, 27, 31) and the Beijing steps page. B's 24-hour retake rule, its penalty wording (1000元以下 for fraud, 2000元以下 for impersonation) and its time arithmetic (3 h of study plus at most 2 h of exams, so at most 5 h) all hold up. A has a wrong fine range (1000–2000 元), a time table whose rows don't add up, and a '2–3 days' pace claim with no source. B is also tighter and says plainly that screen names come from Beijing. A is more complete on the flow (审核 step, face recognition at application) and on the no-prestore and 12-point single-violation points. It is also much longer and spends space on extras, which weighs against it on length. On balance B is slightly better.
